items.title: 14.1.2 Concept of a Vector in Space (Roman Urdu)

blocks.title: Numbering note
blocks.text: Kitab is heading ko 14.1.3 chhaapti hai (Book# 14.1.3). Kitab mein 14.1.1 naam ki koi heading hai hi nahin, is liye portal 14.1 ke sub-headings ko tarteeb se 14.1.1 se 14.1.8 tak number karta hai. Yahan 14.1.2 wahi hai jo kitab mein 14.1.3 hai.

Pichhle subtopic mein humne points ko space mein jagah di. Ab sawal yeh hai ke vector (teer) ko space mein numbers se kaise likhein. Jawab bohat khoobsurat hai: har vector ko origin se shuru karke ek point tak pohanchne wala teer bana lo, phir us point ke teen coordinates hi vector ke teen components ban jaate hain. Chaliye kitab ki baat qadam ba qadam samajhte hain.

Set \(R^{3} = \{(x, y, z) : x, y, z \in R\}\) ko 3-dimensional space kehte hain. \(R^{3}\) ka har element \((x, y, z)\) ek point \(P(x, y, z)\) ko dikhata hai, jo apne coordinates \(x\), \(y\) aur \(z\) se uniquely (sirf ek hi tareeqe se) tay hota hai. Agar space mein koi vector \(\underline{u}\) diya ho, to space mein ek aur sirf ek point \(P(x, y, z)\) aisa hota hai ke vector \(\underline{OP}\) bilkul \(\underline{u}\) ke barabar ho (figure dekhiye). Is tarah har element \((x, y, z) \in R^{3}\) ek unique ordered triple \((x, y, z)\) se jura hai, jo yeh vector dikhata hai:

blocks.text_alt: u equals vector OP equals x, y, z

blocks.alt: Axes x, y, z from O. An arrow labelled u goes from O to the point P(x, y, z). Dashed lines show the coordinates: a vertical dashed line of length z from P down to the xy-plane, and dashed lines of lengths x and y from its foot parallel to the axes.
blocks.caption: The vector u = OP from the origin to the point P(x, y, z) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Set notation ko parhna: \(R^{3} = \{(x, y, z) : x, y, z \in R\}\) ka matlab hai \"woh saari triples \((x, y, z)\) jin ke teenon numbers real hon\". Yani \(R^{3}\) sirf space ka naam hai. Colon \(:\) ko \"aisi ke\" parhiye.
Kyun: har vector \([x, y, z]\) ki shakal mein kyun likha ja sakta hai? Vector kahin bhi banaya ja sakta hai, sirf lambai aur simt maayne rakhti hai. Usay baghair ghumaaye khiskaiye yahan tak ke us ki dum (tail) \(O\) par aa jaaye. Ab us ka sira (head) ek aur sirf ek point \(P(x, y, z)\) par hoga, aur yeh teen numbers vector ko poori tarah bata dete hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Point hai ya vector? Gol brackets \((x, y, z)\) point batate hain (ek jagah); square brackets \([x, y, z]\) vector batate hain (ek harkat ya safar). Same teen numbers dono matlab de sakte hain: \(P(2, 3, 5)\) ek jagah hai aur \([2, 3, 5]\) woh safar hai jo \(O\) se us jagah tak le jaata hai.
Misaal: \((1, 1, 1)\) se \((3, 4, 6)\) tak ka vector x mein \(3 - 1 = 2\), y mein \(4 - 1 = 3\) aur z mein \(6 - 1 = 5\) chalta hai, is liye woh \([2, 3, 5]\) hai. Origin par khiskaane se us ka sira \(P(2, 3, 5)\) par aata hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\((2, 0, 1)\) se \((5, 4, 1)\) tak jaane wala vector kya hai, aur origin par laane ke baad us ka sira kis point par hoga?
Jawab: \([5 - 2,\ 4 - 0,\ 1 - 1] = [3, 4, 0]\); sira \(P(3, 4, 0)\) par, jo xy-plane mein hai kyunke z-component sifar hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: (Hamari practice.) Ek drone zameen par khare aadmi (origin) se 30 m mashriq (x), 40 m shumaal (y) aur 20 m upar (z) par hai. Aadmi se drone tak ka position vector \([30, 40, 20]\) hai, aur drone ka point \(P(30, 40, 20)\). Agar drone 10 m aur upar chala jaaye to sirf z-component badlega: \([30, 40, 30]\). Is se samajh aata hai ke vector ka har component apni simt ki alag kahani sunata hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
\(R^{3}\) real numbers ki saari ordered triples ka set hai: yahi 3-dimensional space hai.
Har point \(P(x, y, z)\) ki sirf ek coordinate triple hoti hai.
Space ka har vector \(\underline{u}\) ek hi \(\underline{OP}\) ke barabar hai, is liye \(\underline{u} = [x, y, z]\).
Gol brackets: point. Square brackets: vector.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
Point \(P(x, y, z)\) aur vector \([x, y, z]\) ko ek hi cheez samajhna; numbers same hain lekin cheezein alag.
Yeh samajhna ke vector hamesha \(O\) se hi shuru hota hai: \([x, y, z]\) us waqt milta hai jab hum usay \(O\) par khiska lein.
Tarteeb badal dena: \([2, 3, 5]\) aur \([3, 2, 5]\) alag vectors hain.
